pool.text: Consider a binary classification problem where the decision boundary is defined by the logistic function \( p(x) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-(\beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2)}} \), which represents the probability of a data point \( \mathbf{x} = (x_1, x_2) \) belonging to class 1. The estimated model parameters are \( \beta_0 = -3 \), \( \beta_1 = 1 \), and \( \beta_2 = -2 \). We are interested in the geometric shape of the classification boundary. The classification boundary occurs where \( p(x) = 0.5 \). Find the equation of this boundary in the \( x_1x_2 \)-plane.
pool.educational_aim: Synthesize Logistic Regression & Classification Boundaries with related mathematical concepts to solve high-difficulty past-paper synthesis, optimization, proof, or modeling problems.
pool.exam_archetype: Logistic Regression & Classification Boundaries — Non-Routine Synthesis & Past-Paper Challenge
pool.sol:
The logistic regression model gives the probability of belonging to class 1 as \( p(x) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-(\beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2)}} \). The classification boundary is the set of points where \( p(x) = 0.5 \).

Setting \( p(x) = 0.5 \), we have:
\( 0.5 = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-(\beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2)}} \)

This implies:
\( 1 + e^{-(\beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2)} = 2 \)

Therefore:
\( e^{-(\beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2)} = 1 \)

Taking the natural logarithm of both sides:
\( -(\beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2) = \ln(1) \)

Since \( \ln(1) = 0 \), we get:
\( \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2 = 0 \)

This is the equation of the linear decision boundary.

Substitute the given parameter values: \( \beta_0 = -3 \), \( \beta_1 = 1 \), and \( \beta_2 = -2 \).

\( -3 + x_1 + (-2) \cdot x_2 = 0 \)

\( -3 + x_1 - 2x_2 = 0 \)

We need to express this in the form \( x_2 = f(x_1) \).

\( 2x_2 = x_1 - 3 \)

\( x_2 = \frac{1}{2} x_1 - \frac{3}{2} \)

This matches choice A.

Setting \( p(x) = 0.5 \), we have: \( 0.5 = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-(\beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2)}} \) This implies: \( 1 + e^{-(\beta_0 + \beta_1 x_1 + \beta_2 x_2)} = 2 \).

pool.text: A binary classification model uses a logistic sigmoid function \( \sigma(z) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-z}} \). The decision boundary is defined by \( \sigma(z) = 0.5 \), where \( z = w_1 x_1 + w_0 \). For a dataset with two features \( x_1 \) and \( x_2 \), the model's linear component is \( z = 2x_1 - x_2 + b \). If the classification boundary passes through the point \( (x_1, x_2) = (3, 1) \), what is the value of the bias \( b \)?

pool.exam_archetype: Logistic Regression & Classification Boundaries — Multi-Step Application & Parameter Solve
pool.sol:
The logistic sigmoid function is \( \sigma(z) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-z}} \). The decision boundary is where \( \sigma(z) = 0.5 \). Setting \( \sigma(z) = 0.5 \) gives \( \frac{1}{1 + e^{-z}} = 0.5 \), which implies \( 1 = 0.5(1 + e^{-z}) \), so \( 2 = 1 + e^{-z} \), and \( e^{-z} = 1 \). This occurs when \( -z = 0 \), or \( z = 0 \). Therefore, the decision boundary is defined by \( z = 0 \).

The linear component of the model is given by \( z = w_1 x_1 + w_2 x_2 + b \). In this problem, \( z = 2x_1 - x_2 + b \).

Since the decision boundary is \( z = 0 \), we have \( 2x_1 - x_2 + b = 0 \).

The classification boundary passes through the point \( (x_1, x_2) = (3, 1) \). Substituting these values into the equation for the decision boundary:
\( 2(3) - 1 + b = 0 \)
\( 6 - 1 + b = 0 \)
\( 5 + b = 0 \)
\( b = -5 \)

pool.text: Consider a centered feature matrix \( \mathbf{X} \) has shape \( N \times 34 \). What is the size and symmetry property of the sample covariance matrix \( \mathbf{\Sigma} = \frac{1}{N-1}\mathbf{X}^T\mathbf{X} \)?

pool.sol: Since \( \mathbf{X} \) has \( 34 \) columns, \( \mathbf{X}^T \) is \( 34 \times N \) and \( \mathbf{X}^T\mathbf{X} \) is \( 34 \times 34 \). Furthermore, \( (\mathbf{X}^T\mathbf{X})^T = \mathbf{X}^T(\mathbf{X}^T)^T = \mathbf{X}^T\mathbf{X} \), proving it is always symmetric.
